title: Slope field, tangent line and separation for dy/dx = x(4 - y)

stimulus.title: Nine points for the slope field of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = x(4 - y)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Consider the differential equation dydx=x(4−y)\frac{dy}{dx} = x(4 - y). On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the equation at the nine points shown.

rubric.point: Slope field: zero slopes at the five points with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4</annotation></semantics></math>; at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math> slopes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1, 1</annotation></semantics></math>; at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3</annotation></semantics></math> slopes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1, 1</annotation></semantics></math>, drawn steeper at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math> than at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
accept: segments whose signs and relative steepness match at all nine points

parts.sample: Slopes: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: 0, 0, 0. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, 0, 1. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>, 0, 2 (for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1, 0, 1</annotation></semantics></math>). Horizontal segments along <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4</annotation></semantics></math>; segments falling to the right at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> and rising at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, steeper on the row <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let y=f(x)y = f(x) be the particular solution to the differential equation with f(2)=3f(2) = 3. Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of ff at x=2x = 2, and use it to approximate f(2.1)f(2.1).

rubric.point: Tangent line: slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{(2, 3)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(4 - 3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3 + 2(x - 2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Approximation: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2.1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3 + 2(0.1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3.2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{(2, 3)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(4 - 3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Tangent line: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3 + 2(x - 2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2.1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3 + 2(0.1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3.2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find d2ydx2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} in terms of xx and yy. Determine whether the approximation in part (b) is an overestimate or an underestimate of f(2.1)f(2.1). Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ x\left(-\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y) - x^2(4 - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y)(1 - x^2)</annotation></semantics></math>.
accept: (4 - y) - x(dy/dx), with dy/dx replaced by x(4 - y)
the unsimplified product-rule form with dy/dx substituted

rubric.point: Overestimate, with reason: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (1)(1 - 4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -3 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down near <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and lies below its tangent line.
accept: overestimate because f is concave down on [2, 2.1]
overestimate because the second derivative is negative there

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{d}{dx}\left[x(4 - y)\right]</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y) - x\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y) - x^2(4 - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4 - y)(1 - x^2)</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 3)</annotation></semantics></math> this is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1)(-3) = -3 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down there, so it lies below the tangent line, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.2</annotation></semantics></math> is an overestimate of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2.1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find y=f(x)y = f(x), the particular solution to the differential equation with the initial condition f(2)=3f(2) = 3.

rubric.point: Antiderivatives: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\ln|4 - y| = \frac{x^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (both sides correct).

Constant of integration and uses the initial condition: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\ln|4 - 3| = 2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = -2</annotation></semantics></math>.
accept: C found from f(2) = 3, consistent with the student's antiderivatives

rubric.point: Solves for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 4 - e^{2 - x^2/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{4 - y} = x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\ln|4 - y| = \frac{x^2}{2} + C</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\ln 1 = 2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = -2</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|4 - y| = 2 - \frac{x^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|4 - y| = e^{2 - x^2/2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - y = 1 > 0</annotation></semantics></math> at the initial point, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - y = e^{2 - x^2/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 4 - e^{2 - x^2/2}</annotation></semantics></math> for all real <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.
